key_insight: A precision-first, physics-checked literature pipeline builds electro-optic property datasets that support prediction for materials excluded from training.
engineering_relevance: The approach could guide electro-optic material selection for optical modulators and microwave-to-optical quantum links across composition and operating conditions.
method: Acquire relevant literature and extract values using layout-aware LLMs and deterministic table parsers.
Apply three-tier verification, normalize notation, reject symmetry-forbidden components, and retain provenance.
Consolidate cross-paper values using median and median absolute deviation, then audit a noise-robust surrogate with leave-one-material-out testing.
evidence_signal: From 49 papers, 414 of 816 candidates were accepted; exact-match precision/recall were 0.51/0.48 against 303 certified values, while held-out baseline wins rose from 1/4 to 9/13 as coverage grew from 10 to 22 materials.
watch_item: Exact-record accuracy remains modest, and the uncontrolled database-growth comparison does not establish that curation caused improved generalization.
paper_title: From Autonomous Knowledge Generation to Generalizable Property Prediction: A Precision-First Pipeline for Electro-Optic Materials Discovery
